title: Europe before the war
hook: A diplomatic map and the decisions that unravelled it.
notes: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed. Sources by scene: 1. A snapshot before the annexations: https://icr.ethz.ch/data/cshapes/; 2. Austria is annexed: https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/nazi-territorial-aggression-the-anschluss; 3. Munich changes Czechoslovakia’s position: https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/timeline-event/holocaust/1933-1938/munich-agreement; 4. A pact made in Moscow: https://encyclopedia.ushmm.org/content/en/article/the-soviet-union-and-the-eastern-front CShapes 2.0 snapshot date 1 January 1938, before Anschluss and Munich. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; it encodes diplomatic state/dependency boundaries and omits small changes. Later event scenes do not redraw those borders.

scenes.title: A snapshot before the annexations
scenes.text: CShapes records state boundaries on 1 January 1938. Austria and Czechoslovakia still appear separately. This is diplomatic geography before the year’s annexations, not a map of the eve of war in September 1939.

scenes.title: Austria is annexed
scenes.text: German troops entered Austria on 12 March 1938; the Anschluss law incorporated it into Nazi Germany the following day. Vienna locates the annexation. No new territorial polygon is inferred from this point.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1938 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)

scenes.title: Munich changes Czechoslovakia’s position
scenes.text: The agreement reached at Munich on 29–30 September 1938 allowed German annexation of the Sudetenland. The city point locates the negotiations; it does not draw the affected border districts.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1938 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)

scenes.title: A pact made in Moscow
scenes.text: Germany and the Soviet Union signed their non-aggression pact on 23 August 1939. Its secret protocol divided spheres in eastern Europe and provided for Poland’s partition. The Moscow point locates the agreement, not its territorial clauses.
scenes.stamp: Borders as of 1 Jan 1938 · CShapes 2.0 (legal states, not occupation)
